raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I don’t like making big changes. On my 14.5 mu, I’ll still do wheat and then maize after it, same as always. This land feeds us, so I first think about not missing the season and not letting the crop go hungry. Fertilizer costs money, water from the well also costs money, but if I save too much and the crop turns weak, that loss is worse. I cannot do fancy calculations. I look at how the field did last year, whether the soil still has strength, and what the other people nearby are doing. Wheat needs steady care through winter and spring, and maize must go in fast after wheat harvest because the time is tight. Since there are only 2 people in my house, I keep the work simple, use the same kinds of seed I know, put fertilizer in round amounts, and irrigate when the ground is really dry or when the crop is at an important stage.

decision.reasoning_summary: I keep wheat-maize on all 14.5 mu because that is what I know and it spreads the risk across the year. I do not dare cut fertilizer too much because if the crop turns yellow or thin, I lose more grain than the money I save. But I also cannot throw money around, so I use moderate amounts, mostly the same as years when the harvest was decent. Wheat gets more water because spring drought can hurt it badly, and maize I mostly rely on summer rain unless it turns dry. Since only two of us are at home, I use machine help for the busy times, especially wheat harvest and maize planting, so I do not miss the season.
